summary: Device token selection and speculative verification under Core's whole sampling law: bias, suppression and penalties over committed plus staged outputs, temperature, top-k, top-p and min-p over the full vocabulary, Core's seeded counter-based draws, and rejection-sampling predictions for the device accept kernel
implementation_scope: CUDA full-vocabulary law per (request, column) row: Core's steps 2 to 5 into a scratch row, then top-k, top-p and the draw as sort-free rank-prefix searches over orderable keys (eight 4-bit digit passes plus an id-order tie scan) with fixed-order FP32/FP64 sums; enqueue_sample with a chosen DrawPurpose and optional dense law output; enqueue_verify writing accept, residual and bonus predictions for greedy (one-hot) or sampled drafts; enqueue_commit for device-held counts and positions; the two-stage top-64 selection kept for 1 <= top_k <= 64 and routed on the device; a constraint-bitmask kernel. An FP64 Python mirror uses Core's draw bit for bit. Engine supplied: target and draft logits on the device, Request storage and history initialization, scratch and the round structure.

agent_guidance.use_when: Logits are produced on the device and requests sample (temperature, top-k, top-p, min-p, penalties, bias), especially when sampled requests should draft and verify inside a captured decode graph
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Only greedy decoding is served and the existing argmax path already matches plain greedy bit for bit, or per-token selection cost is measured to dominate a round and no split-row adaptation is planned
provides: Rank order by processed value with lowest-index tie-break; greedy path
Core's steps 2 to 5 on the device: bias and bans, min_tokens suppression, repetition over prompt and outputs, frequency and presence over committed plus staged outputs
Full-vocabulary top-k, top-p and min-p and one draw per token as sort-free prefix searches, deterministic for a given vocabulary
Two-stage top-64 selection for 1 <= top_k <= 64, chosen on the device so one captured launch serves every request
Core's Philox draw on the device with sample, draft, accept and residual purposes at each output position
Rejection-sampling verification predictions for greedy or sampled drafts that the device greedy accept kernel consumes unchanged
Dense law rows for a sampled drafter's q
Device commits of output counts and positions from a device-held emitted count
FP64 Python mirror of processing, law, draw and verification with Core's bit-identical draw
A kernel applying a structured-output bitmask (Core's TokenMatcher::allowed_bits) to logit rows before selection
engine_supplies: Target and draft logits as FP32 rows on the device, and the scratch rows
Per-sequence Request from crit::core::resolve_sampling with merged, sorted bias ids, position set to the committed output count, and counts/prompt_seen built from TokenHistory
The device round: commit as the first Forward kernel, drafting, verify writing logits, then the device greedy accept kernel
Keeping greedy requests on their existing argmax path where bit identity matters
preserve: Rank order with index tie-break and Core's processing order
One draw per emitted token from Core's uniform at its own seed, stream, output position and purpose
Each verify or draft column counts the drafts staged before it
Acceptance with u * q(d) < p(d) under the processed target law p and the law q the draft was drawn from; residual from max(p - q, 0); bonus from the last column
Fixed-order sums so repeated identical requests give identical tokens
adapt: Block size, digit width and splitting a row over several blocks
Fusing selection into the head or the verify epilogue
Sparse draft laws instead of dense q rows, keeping the complete residual

code_files.purpose: Params, Request, Rows and Verify; selection, mask, sample, verify and commit launch interfaces
Two-stage top-64 selection, the full-vocabulary law (processing, prefix searches, draw), rejection-sampling verification, commits and constraint masking
FP64 Python mirror of processing, law, draw and verification with Core's Philox draw and a runnable example

requires.hardware: CUDA C++20 and Core's sampling header (crit::core) for the device path; Python 3.11+ standard library for the mirror
requires.model: One logits row per selected token or verify column; drafter and target share token ids
requires.workload: Generation that samples with Core's rules, with or without speculative drafts, and needs reproducible seeds

contract.input: Device logits rows and vocabulary size; device Params or Requests; staged drafts per column; optional draft law rows; scratch of scratch_floats(vocab, rows) floats (selection: 256 x 64 candidates)
contract.output: Selected tokens or verify predictions in device memory (-1 when nothing is selectable); optional dense law rows; Params.position advanced by one per selection; commits advance Request.position and counts
contract.ownership: The engine owns logits, Params, Requests and their arrays, scratch and outputs; kernels borrow them on the caller's stream until it reaches them
contract.failure: Null pointers, an empty vocabulary, short strides or too many requests are rejected at launch; NaN and +inf logits are not filtered; FP32 values and weights can pick a neighbouring token when a draw lands within rounding of a boundary
contract.core_boundary: Sampling rules, the draw and the host sampler are Core's (crit/sampling.h: uniform, DrawPurpose, SamplingParams, resolve_sampling, TokenHistory, Sampler); this entry is the device path of steps 2 to 5 and 7 to 12 plus speculative verification. Engines report support through ModelInfo::sampling and read SamplingOptions in Model::open_request

dependencies: Python standard library for the mirror

validation.host: Core's sampling fixture covers the rules, the generator and Sampler; the Python mirror is checked against Core's Philox vectors and Sampler draws, greedy ties, nucleus membership, top-k/top-p reductions, Core's processing order, the uncapped full vocabulary, min-p, and verification that keeps the target law for greedy and sampled drafts over 6,000 seeds
validation.native: Selection: greedy ties, top-k 1 and tiny top-p reducing to greedy, position advance and repeatability, draws equal to crit::core::Sampler::sample away from boundaries and frequencies within four standard errors; masks equal the host's -inf pattern. Law: dense law equal to Sampler::distribution with bias, bans, suppression, repetition, frequency and presence over staged columns, top-k, top-p and min-p; top_k 0 draws inside Core's interval over 50,000 tokens and mostly beyond rank 64; verify columns equal to the rejection rule with Core's accept, residual and sample draws away from boundaries; first emitted tokens follow the target law for greedy and sampled drafts over 16,384 seeds; commits of counts and positions
validation.performance: No throughput or output-quality claim; the full law is reference speed with one block per row
